key_insight: BioMedVR adapts pretrained vision-language models to biomedical images with compact visual reprogramming while reducing class confusion using positive and negative prompt experts.
clinical_relevance: This could help build more accurate, data-efficient diagnostic classifiers for biomedical imaging when labeled medical data are limited.
method: Injects learnable visual reprogramming modules to adapt CLIP-like models with few shots.
Uses confusion-aware attributes plus a confusion-suppression loss to reduce false-positive matches.
Combines a positive expert and negative expert with adaptive gating in a mixture-of-prompt-experts design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports superior accuracy and generalization on 18 datasets, including 11 biomedical datasets and 7 natural-image benchmarks.
watch_item: Results are from benchmark evaluation, so real-world clinical deployment would still need external validation, robustness testing, and workflow integration checks.
paper_title: BioMedVR: Confusion-Aware Mixture-of-Prompt Experts for Biomedical Visual Reprogramming
